messages.author: 2d974991cab5f3a7
messages.subject: if statement in the parameters block
parts:
Dear All,
Hi

Does not work if statement in the parameters block? Please see the below code (or run the attached file in R):

data 
{
int<lower=1> n;
real x[n];
int<lower=1> dist;
}
parameters 
{
// Beta distribution
if(dist == 1)
{
real<lower=0> alpha;
real<lower=0> beta;
}
// Kumaraswamy distribution
if(dist == 2)
{
real<lower=0> alpha;
real<lower=0> beta;
}
// PowerBeta distribution
if(dist == 3)
{
real<lower=0> alpha;
real<lower=0> beta;
real<lower=0,upper=min(x)> theta;
real<lower=0> k;
}
}
model 
{
// Beta distribution
if(dist == 1)
{
x ~ beta(alpha,beta);
}
// Kumaraswamy distribution
if(dist == 2)
{
real s;
s = 0;
for(i in 1:n) s = s + log1m(pow(x,alpha));
traget += n*(log(alpha) + log(beta))+(alpha-1)*sum(log(x))+(beta-1)*s;
}
// PowerBeta distribution
if(dist == 3)
{
s = 0;
for(i in 1:n) s = s + log1m(pow(theta/x[i],k));
target += = n*(log(k) + k*beta*log(theta) - lbeta(alpha,beta)) + (alpha-1)*s - (k*beta+1)*sum(log(x));
}
}


-Bistoon

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] if statement in the parameters block
parts:
More pedantically, a Stan program defines a log probability density
proportional to pi( params | data ). If the definition of the params
changes then you’re defining a different density which requires a
different Stan program.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] if statement in the parameters block
parts:
But the parameters depend on the data in terms of size. So
what Stephen was suggesting was a hack where the parameters
are

real foo1[N1];
real foo2[N2];
real foo3[N3];

You can "select" which parameters to use by setting N1 = 0 and N2 = 0 to
give you foo3, etc. So we always have vectors foo1, foo2, and foo3, but
sometimes one of them is empty.

- Bob
